subject: Buying roles clarification + legal checklist (post-demo)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@finserve.com>, Tom Bradley <tom.bradley@finserve.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Buying roles clarification + legal checklist (post-demo)

Hi Elena & Tom — thanks again for your time earlier today. Quick recap and a few asks so we keep momentum:  

- Demo highlights: Redwood hosted inference + Dedicated option, can meet the 150ms token latency target for your bursty trade-alert pipeline; prefix caching should cover ~85% of predictable prompts.
- Open questions we need to lock down before procurement: economic buyer name/approval path, security contact for SOC2/pseudonymization requirements, and whether procurement needs a PO vs. Coupa/eProcurement flow.

Can you confirm:  
1) Who will sign off on the purchase (economic buyer)?
2) Who on your side will own the security/compliance checklist and evidence (SOC2, key rotation, audit logs)?
3) Procurement timeline (standard 30-day review, or longer due to enterprise compliance)?

Attached is a short risk checklist template we use for initial reads — feel free to forward to your security team. If useful, we can schedule a 30-min security deep-dive this week.

Next internal steps on our side once we get answers: Rishi to prepare draft commercial (term sheet + SAML/KMS options), Markus to start legal intake and redline plan, Priya to map deployment options and region constraints.

Thanks — Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
Attachment: FinServe_Risk_Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@finserve.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bradley <tom.bradley@finserve.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Buying roles clarification + legal checklist (post-demo)

Thanks, Olga — great session. A few clarifications from our side:  

- Economic buyer: Marcus Dell, CFO (marcus.dell@finserve.com). He will need a short business case (cost vs. expected reduction in latency-related incidents) and the indicative TCO.
- Security/compliance lead: Sarah Lee (sarah.lee@finserve.com) will own the checklist and coordinate evidence requests (SOC2 report, data residency details, encryption/KMS info). I’ve copied Tom — he’s procurement and will want to understand billing model (usage vs committed).
- Procurement flow: we use Coupa for orders but procurement reviews usually take 3–4 weeks; legal redlines often take an additional 1–2 weeks for vendors with unusual data access. If we can provide a limited-scope MSA + SOW and a short appendix on data handling, that speeds review.

I’ve attached the initial completed risk checklist with a few notations (red flags on KMS expectations). Happy to set up the security call, Sarah is available Thu 9–11am PT.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Gomez
Program Director, Platform Integrations — FinServe Financial
Attachment: FinServe_Risk_Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

Thumbs up on owners — I’ll run the legal intake and ask for the following from FinServe ahead of the call:  

- Confirmation of required data residency (region and retention) and whether they require us to flow-down KMS/HSM details.
- Any procurement standard clauses that must be included in the MSA (e.g., subcontractor flow-down, SLA credits, indemnities).

I’ve attached the multi-org mandate we sometimes send (covers multi-tenant vs dedicated deployment guardrails) — I’ll pre-fill the sections we can and highlight where we need FinServe specifics. Expect a redline window of ~5 business days after their legal provides comments; if they push heavy IP/data constraints that could extend review.

Markus
